summary: auth-service began returning 401 invalid_token for ~36% of token validations starting ~14:00-14:02Z on 2026-04-15. Two changes landed within 2 minutes of each other and of the onset: deployment dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten, at 14:00:00Z) and config change cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id rotated k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04, at 14:01:00Z). All infrastructure signals are clean (auth-service CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, no restarts, latency flat ~90ms; redis-cache and user-db healthy), ruling out resource/infrastructure/dependency causes. Auth-service's own logs are unsearchable (log-pipeline outage), so the decisive discriminator between the two code/config candidates is unavailable. Both historical analogues exist (HIST-108 key-rotation/partial JWKS; HIST-109 JWT library upgrade). The evidence cannot separate the deployment from the key rotation, so the outcome is inconclusive.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade deploy (dep-5710) broke token validation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service v7.3.0 (dep-5710, 14:00:00Z) replaced jjwt 0.11 with 0.12 (breaking parser API) and rewrote TokenValidator; the new parser path rejects previously valid tokens, producing 401 invalid_token for a stable ~36% of /token/validate calls. Mirrors HIST-109 (library upgrade changed clock-skew default).

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deployed auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z with 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'
New validator rejects a subset of tokens -> 401 invalid_token from 14:02:22Z
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~36% at 14:00Z bucket

assumptions: The rewritten parser/clock-skew default is actually stricter and rejects real live tokens
dep-5710 pods serve the failing fraction while others serve fine (or a specific token class is rejected)

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) caused tokens to fail validation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Automatic signing-key rotation at 14:01:00Z changed jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 before all auth-service pods loaded the new key material in their JWKS, so tokens signed/validated against the stale key are rejected, yielding 401 invalid_token for a subset of requests. Mirrors HIST-108.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z
Pods with stale/absent new key reject tokens -> 401 invalid_token from 14:02:22Z
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~36% at 14:00Z bucket

assumptions: Key rotation is not announced to validation pods before the key_id switch
The ~36% fraction reflects a pod/key-pool split rather than a token class

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / infrastructure failure in auth-service or its datastores
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service 401 spike caused by CPU/memory/connection exhaustion, pod restarts, or redis/user-db degradation.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: auth-service cpu_pct ~38%, memory_pct ~52%, restarts=0, latency flat ~90ms; redis hit_ratio ~96%, memory ~69%; user-db slow_queries ~0.3 — all flat across onset (F5, F7).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation from traffic surge
ranked_hypotheses.statement: 401 spike caused by request-rate growth outpacing auth-service capacity.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat at ~400 req/s and rate_limited_per_min ~2 across onset (F6); latency unchanged.

assumptions: The 401s originate in auth-service token validation (the gateway WARN message names auth-service POST /token/validate returning invalid_token).
No third change (e.g., a secret/token expiry or JWKS distribution job) exists outside the deployments and config-changes tools I queried for the 06:00-15:59Z window.
The uniform ~36% failure fraction can be produced by either a token-class rejection or a partial pod/key-pool split; I could not verify which.
reduce: the metric 'error_rate' buckets are 900s wide, so onset is bounded to within the 14:00:00Z bucket, not to the minute.

timeline.event: dep-5710 deploys auth-service v7.3.0 (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API; TokenValidator rewritten)
auth-service error_rate bucket jumps to 31.81%; api-gateway error_rate to 17.67%
Incident reported (SEV-1); auth-service logs unavailable due to pipeline outage
Error rate persists ~36% with no rollback of dep-5710

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5710 (auth-service to pre-v7.3.0) as the fastest reversible test; if 401s stop within one deploy window, H1 is confirmed.
recommended_actions.rationale: Deploy is the top-ranked candidate and is cleanly reversible; it is the single most informative action.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback does not restore service, re-publish the previous key (k-2025-10) / verify JWKS propagation across all auth-service pods for cfg-2705.
recommended_actions.rationale: Key rotation is the equally-plausible alternative (H2) and mirrors HIST-108; staggered key distribution would leave a stable failing fraction.

recommended_actions.action: Restore/reroute the identity-namespace log pipeline so auth-service token-validation error detail (signature vs parse/format vs expired) is searchable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The validator's own error message is the decisive discriminator between a parser bug and a key mismatch and is currently unavailable.

recommended_actions.action: Compare the set of failing vs succeeding tokens (issuing pod/key id, iat/exp, algorithm) against the new parser and key pool to isolate which change rejects them.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes a token-class rejection (parser/H1) from a pod/key-pool split (rotation/H2).

recommended_actions.action: Decouple future JWT library upgrades and signing-key rotations from the same maintenance window, and gate key rotation on confirmed JWKS propagation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both candidate triggers landed within 2 minutes, making attribution and rollback ambiguous.

data_gaps: auth-service validator logs are unsearchable (log-pipeline outage): the exact rejection reason (signature failure vs parser/format error vs expiry/clock-skew) — the single best discriminator between H1 and H2 — is unavailable.
No per-pod / per-instance breakdown of auth-service error_rate, so a pod-level split (key-pool only loaded on some pods) cannot be confirmed or excluded.
No data on JWKS key-distribution timing or which key_id each pod currently trusts.
No visibility into whether the failing 36% correlates with tokens issued before 14:00 vs after, nor with a specific signing key/algorithm.
Cannot confirm whether dep-5710 and cfg-2705 were intended to ship together (change-management/CI context), which would explain the 1-minute offset.

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) was ~0.2% through 13:45Z, then jumped to 31.81% in the 14:00Z bucket and held ~36% through the end of data.
api-gateway WARN logs show 466 occurrences of the pattern 'auth-service POST /v<n>/token/validate -> <n> invalid_token', first seen 2026-04-15T14:02:22Z.

Deployment dep-5710 changed auth-service to v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z, described as 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation' with changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; it is live and not rolled back.

findings.statement: A single config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z ('Scheduled signing-key rotation').
auth-service resource metrics are flat across the onset: cpu_pct ~38%, memory_pct ~52%, latency_p99_ms ~90ms, and restarts constant 0 — no resource or restart anomaly.
auth-service request_rate is unchanged across the onset (~400 req/s), so the 401 spike is not load-driven; rate_limited_per_min is also flat at ~2.
Downstream shared components are healthy: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct ~96% and memory_pct ~69%; user-db slow_queries_per_min ~0.3 — no dependency degradation coinciding with onset.
api-gateway error_rate tracks auth-service: ~0.2% through 13:48Z, then ~21% from the 14:00Z bucket onward, with gateway latency_p99 unchanged (~210ms).

auth-service logs could not be retrieved for the incident window — the query tool returned 'backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)' on repeated attempts, consistent with the reported log-pipeline outage for the identity namespace.
No 401s are attributable to gateway-side filtering: api-gateway ERROR-level logs in 14:00-15:59Z matched 0 entries, so the auth failures surface as WARN-level pass-through of auth-service responses.

Historical incidents include both a key-rotation 401 case (HIST-108: 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') and a JWT-library-upgrade 401 case (HIST-109: JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default) — i.e., both current candidates have precedent.

JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default

findings.statement: Inference: the auth-service failure is a code/config-level token-validation fault, not load, resource exhaustion, infrastructure, or a datastore/dependency failure, because all non-code signals (CPU, memory, restarts, latency, redis, user-db, request_rate) are flat and only the deploy/config timestamps align with onset.
